text:
morgan: Heads up — I just reproduced a permissions gap in the rollout UI. Canaries can be aborted by users who have the deploy.override role even if they don't have canary.abort. Repro steps below, this is actionable and low blast radius but counts as an access-control bug.

morgan: Repro steps:
1) Start canary via API (successful)
2) UI user with deploy.override aborts canary -> abort accepted
3) check service logs: controller accepted abort without checking canary.abort permission.

morgan: logs:
```
2026-03-19T18:12:03Z controller=canary action=abort user=ops_jane result=200 req_id=abcd1234
2026-03-19T18:12:03Z authz service=rbac check=SKIPPED reason=role_override_present req_id=abcd1234
```

deploy-bot: deploy:canary #789 by @ops_jane -> aborted (duration 4m) :warning:

aisling: ugh. do we know where the bypass happened? UI layer or controller?

morgan: looks like the controller has a short-circuit for "override roles" to let SREs stop rollouts quickly. That short-circuit doesn't re-evaluate canary-specific permissions (canary.abort). RBAC policy: we intended override to be able to escalate, but we forgot to log the exact grant and we didn't restrict it to people on the incident roster.

sam: also spotted something else — the abort path uses a fallback creds token stored encrypted with KMS. The KMS key's iam policy permits encrypt/decrypt for service-account:sre-runner and for role deploy.override group. If the UI actor is in that group, the controller will decrypt and proceed. So two things: missing fine-grained canary permission check + KMS scope too broad.

sam: config snippet from controller auth check (simplified):
```
if user.has_role('deploy.override'):
    allow_abort()  # missing per-resource permission check
else:
    check('canary.abort')
```

laura: can we get an immediate mitigation? probably restrict deploy.override to incident roster and rotate the KMS key used by fallback creds.

infra-oncall: on it — I'll push a quick RBAC change to remove deploy.override from the broader ops group and add a temporary deny rule for canary.abort to non-roster accounts. Rolling now, ETA 10m. PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/rbac/pulls/2345

security-bot: Created issue SEC-2026: "canary abort bypass via deploy.override + KMS scope". Priority P2. Added runbook link: https://intra.redwood/sec/runbooks/canary-authz.md

morgan: For triage: we need to confirm audit logs captured the decision and which principal actually triggered the abort. Current controller logs show req_id but authz decision line is terse. We should add structured audit fields: principal, roles_evaluated, why_short_circuit.

aisling: Agreed. Also add a test in the policy suite to assert that deploy.override alone cannot abort canaries unless explicit incident tag present.

sam: KMS follow-up: narrow the key IAM to only the service account and remove the deploy.override binding. We'll create a rotated key and re-encrypt fallback tokens. I'll open a follow-up PR for KMS changes.

ops_jane: I was the one who aborted the canary — I thought I had incident rights, we did have a page from pagerduty earlier but looks like our group membership is broad. Sorry for the confusion. Happy to help with repro and test once changes land.

laura: thanks @ops_jane. No blame — this is a config+policy gap.

infra-oncall: mitigation rolled out: deploy.override trimmed, deny rule applied. Monitoring alert created for unexpected aborts (SEC-alert-707).

morgan: next steps captured in SEC-2026: 1) tighten KMS IAM, 2) add controller-level canary.abort check even if override present, 3) structured audit logs, 4) test case in policy suite, 5) postmortem notes. I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow 11:00 PT.

security-bot: Linking linked tickets: RBAC PR #2345, KMS PR #2346, controller PR #2347, test PR #2348.

sam: assigning myself KMS PR, morgan owns controller PR, aisling will add tests.

morgan: thanks — keeping this thread to record the quick blameless triage. :thumbsup:
